# A sparkline's data update goes unpainted for 10 s on the dense Workstation control

## Context

Promoted from the 2026-09-23 09:14Z defect-note after it became the dense Workstation control's dominant red: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` — "the real tour keeps density, data, Canvas output, themes, rails, and identities live" — reds at its Canvas receipt (`the exact scale Canvas changes after its worker receives new data`, `expect.poll(readCanvasPixels …).not.toBe(beforePixels)`, 10 s) in 12 of 16 runs today, the last 9 in a row (10:2x–10:45Z), on `dev@5424760c03`…`231e4e64a8` plus PR #19109's six-line reconciler change, headless Chromium 1280×800 on the seat's own Neural Link bridge. The first three runs of the day (08:50–08:57Z) passed it. With that one poll softened, the same tour runs green end to end (3/3), so the red is confined to this receipt.

## The Problem

The receipt asks the Canvas Worker's paint to change after the App Worker receives new data. Measured in instrumented runs (10:03–10:35Z): `pulseScaleSparkline(target)` returns its receipt and the target sparkline's App-worker `values` differ within ~80 ms of the call, every run; the on-glass `canvas.screenshot()` stays byte-identical for the full 10 s in the failing runs. The canvas element is the same DOM node throughout the test (a `Set` tagged at boot), `getContext('2d')` throws `InvalidStateError` on it (its control is transferred, as expected), it is connected, visible, 139 px wide; no console error or pageerror. So the data path is live and the paint path is not — for that sparkline, for at least 10 s.

Observation vs inference: the unpainted update is observed; which side stops — the renderer never scheduling a frame for that item, or a frame drawn into a bitmap the compositor no longer presents — is not classified.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/canvas/Sparkline.mjs` is the Canvas Worker's singleton renderer: one `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`renderLoop`, :302) drives every registered item; sparse animation pulses one visible chart at a time, and adaptive backpressure snaps a data update instead of morphing it under load (Vega's 2026-06-04 read of the file; the operator's 2026-02-10 note on cell sparklines animating during scroll).
- The receipt's target is the first scale sparkline whose App-side `offscreenRegistered` is true (`readScaleSparklines`, :276); right before the pulse the test sets `usePulse: false, useTransition: false` on it and waits 150 ms (:1495–1499). A snap update on an item that neither pulses nor transitions depends on the loop still visiting it — a lead, not a cause.
- The witness is a Neural Link spec (deselected in CI), so the red is seen only on seats running it locally — every seat running the dense control today.
- Falsified: a 400 ms held press on the dock splitter does not stop the sparklines painting (four pulses of `neo-sparkline-1` repainted in 246–264 ms, 09:11Z), so the #19086 test-side settle reads are not the cause; those receipts landed before the failure rate rose.

## Classification (2026-09-23, instrumented dense-tour runs 10:53–11:04Z on the seat's own bridge)

**The update was painted — it was the same picture.** Receipts from inside the Canvas Worker for the exact pulse the receipt makes: `updateData` found the target item (139×45 bitmap, `activeItems` no, stress 1.04), took the snap branch and drew; the component received that receipt in 2 ms; the canvas stayed the same node in the same row (a `MutationObserver` on the pane saw zero removals or insertions around the pulse), connected and in view. The bitmap's own checksum (a sampled `getImageData` sum) read **12500 before and 12500 after the draw** — the new values produced the identical picture — and a second pulse changed it (→ 11661) and the glass at once.

Why the picture repeats: `pulseScaleSparkline` (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`) built the trend from `((feed.sequence + point * 5) % 9) - 4`, and the seed (`apps/workstation/store/Scale.mjs`) from `((index * 3 + point * 5) % 9) - 4` — one family of nine cyclic delta patterns (each a twelve-point window of the same nine-cycle). The sparkline normalises its values to the cell, so a picture is its deltas: record 1 (index 0, the receipt's usual target) repaints identically whenever the feed sequence is a multiple of nine at the pulse. The pulse lands at a near-constant sequence after boot (10 records/s), so the collision is timing-locked — #19086's press and settle fixes shifted the test onto the colliding sequence, which is why the rate rose from 0 of 3 to 12 of 16 in one morning. The title's "unpainted" was the receipt's reading, not the mechanism.

Falsified on the way: a missing worker item (found every time); a remount after transfer (`offscreenRegistered` true, no DOM churn); the loop not visiting a non-animating item (the snap branch draws synchronously); the #19086 settle reads and a held splitter press (09:11Z: four pulses repainted in ~250 ms while `usePulse` was still on). Found on the way, real and unit-proven, but not this receipt's cause: the renderer's loop overwrote a snap update that arrived while a transition was in flight — `renderLoop` recomputes a transitioning item's values from its old start and target every tick and lands on the old target (`src/canvas/Sparkline.mjs`, transition block). Noted for a future witness: `DomAccess.transferCanvasToWorker` swallows a remounted canvas's second `transferControlToOffscreen()` (`:1433`) and `worker/Canvas.mjs#unregisterCanvas` deletes the retrievable window map, so a remounted sparkline could never paint again.

## The Fix

`pulseScaleSparkline` advances its pattern offset until the new trend's deltas differ from the record's current trend (`Workspace.sameSparklineShape`: same length, same deltas) — the nine shifts are distinct windows, so at most one can collide. The renderer's snap branch retires an in-flight transition before it draws (and drops a pulse-less item from the loop's active set). Two unit arms: a borrowed-prototype pulse with a feed sequence that collides with record 1's seed on purpose, and the renderer's loop driven by hand against a stand-in canvas. The dense witness is the runtime receipt: the Canvas assertion green in three consecutive runs of the tracked spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The cause is classified from Canvas-Worker evidence (item found / drawn / bitmap changed) and recorded here. *Restated 2026-09-23: not a stall — the bitmap was drawn and unchanged because the picture repeated.*
- [ ] AC-2 `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` "the real tour keeps density…" passes its Canvas receipt in three consecutive runs on `dev`, unmodified apart from what the classification requires.
- [ ] AC-3 A pulse never repaints the record's current shape, and a snap update on a sparkline with `usePulse: false, useTransition: false` survives the next loop tick — unit arms on `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` and `src/canvas/Sparkline.mjs`, both red before their fix. *Restated 2026-09-23 from "painted within one loop tick", which the classification showed was never the gap.*

## Out of Scope

- #19094 / PR #19109 (the overflow control frame) and #19086 / PR #19095 (the press and monitor fixes) — the tour reaches this receipt because of them, and they do not touch the renderer.
- #19103 (a canvas worker per window group) — a different problem on the same worker.
